chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And whatever you give as usury so that it may increase in the wealth of the people, it does not increase with Allah.
He said: It is your gift to a man by which you seek from him a return better than it; that is a usury which is consumed.

key_terms.الثَّوَابَ: a return or recompense expected in exchange
key_terms.رِبًا: usury; gain sought through increase in wealth
key_terms.هَدِيَّتُكَ: your gift; something presented to another person
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ: consumed; taken and benefited from as unlawfully gained wealth

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about riba in Surah al-Rum mean according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: The Imam عليه السلام explains the verse as referring to a gift given with the intention of receiving something better in return. Such a transaction outwardly appears as gifting, but in meaning it functions like riba and is described as something consumed as usury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3995 - Ibrahim ibn Umar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)
regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic:
"And whatever you give as usury so that it may increase in the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah (swt)" (Surah Ar-Rum 30:39)
Imam (as) said: "It is your gift to a man through which you seek a better return than it, and that is consumed as usury."
